stories.title: A.P. Moller Capital acquires Mainstream Renewable Power South Africa
stories.summary: A.P. Moller Capital has acquired a South African solar, wind and battery storage developer through its Emerging Markets Infrastructure Fund II. The firm plans to work with existing management to grow the portfolio and move pipeline projects forward. The developer currently holds a development pipeline of 11.9 GW.

stories.title: India targets 15 MMTPA compressed biogas capacity
stories.summary: A CII report suggests India's compressed biogas ambition could replace 37 percent of LNG imports and save $7.7 billion. With only 210 of 838 registered projects commissioned, the sector faces hurdles in execution and feedstock supply. Success depends on the entire output being produced, absorbed and used.

stories.title: Amazon to invest $7 billion in Indian renewable energy
stories.summary: Amazon announced plans to procure $7 billion in renewable energy in India by 2030, adding to $4 billion already contracted. The investment supports a new global goal to reduce the carbon intensity of electricity powering its operations by 65 percent. Every unit of electricity now comes with targets.

stories.title: Institutional campuses and India's conservation network
stories.summary: India joined global signatories at COP15 in agreeing to protect 30 percent of land and coastal areas by 2030. A recent analysis indicates the country's protected area network currently covers roughly 28 percent of its geographical area. The gap remains for institutional campuses to help bridge the difference.

stories.title: West Java backs Monash and UI nature-based water security project - Monash University
Andhra Pradesh reviews green building implementation
stories.summary: Andhra Pradesh officials met in Visakhapatnam to discuss the field-level implementation of green building norms. Managing Director S. Nagalakshmi cited inter-departmental coordination and local technical capacity as crucial for energy efficiency. The state continues to highlight its progress in enhancing energy efficiency across various sectors.

stories.title: Global clean energy transition demands millions of acres, threatening indigenous rights: Report - news - Mongabay
OJK urges banks to finance green building transformation
stories.summary: Indonesia's Financial Services Authority is pushing banks to increase sustainability-linked loan financing. OJK Chief Executive Dian Ediana stated that banks must act as active partners in the real sector's transformation to drive low-carbon investment. Collaboration is described as the key to strengthening the nation's economic growth.

stories.title: Oxford Street redesign looks to Victorian promenades
stories.summary: Architectural firm East is using the concept of the Victorian promenade to inform its redesign of Oxford Street. The approach focuses on walking to frame reality and make existing qualities visible. The firm spent 30 years exploring the relationship between buildings and public space in ordinary territories.

stories.title: IOC gains approval for sustainable aviation fuel supply
stories.summary: Indian Oil Corporation has received government approval to supply sustainable aviation fuel from its Panipat refinery. The facility is capable of meeting India's 1 percent blending mandate for international flights in 2027. The company plans to secure airline supply agreements before investing in additional production plants.

stories.title: Green Bengal Summit discusses climate-resilient urban development
stories.summary: The CII Indian Green Building Council hosted the Green Bengal Summit in Kolkata to address Net Zero pathways and sustainable urbanisation. Government representatives and industry experts discussed climate-resilient development and resource efficiency. The event brought together architects and developers to focus on the future of West Bengal.

stories.title: India's office market records strongest nine months
stories.summary: India's office market saw its strongest nine months on record in 2026. With global companies signing leases for buildings still under construction, developers face pressure to avoid design errors. Project timelines depend on the coordination between architects, structural engineers and contractors once construction is already underway.

stories.title: NAREP Summit to address real estate development
stories.summary: The National Association of Real Estate Professionals will host a summit in New Delhi on 25 November to discuss the next billion square feet of development. Policymakers and developers will engage in dialogue regarding emerging priorities. The sector is currently looking for its next billion square feet.

stories.title: Inside Ananya Birla's Jatia House
stories.summary: Industrialist Kumar Mangalam Birla purchased the Mumbai mansion Jatia House in 2018 for 425 crore rupees. The property features European classical architecture, high ceilings and expansive interiors. It is currently home to Ananya Birla, who resides in the palace-inspired structure featuring massive gardens and artwork.

stories.title: Bengaluru Metro corridor completion delayed to 2033
stories.summary: The Hebbal-Sarjapur Metro corridor in Bengaluru has been delayed from 2031 to April 2033. The project is still awaiting approval from the Union government nearly 22 months after state clearance. The 37.8-km route is intended to connect southeast Bengaluru with the northern part of the city.

stories.title: Gurugram seals 37 properties over land-use violations
stories.summary: The Department of Town and Country Planning sealed 37 properties in Gurugram's DLF Phase 2 following a three-day crackdown. The establishments, including supermarkets and clinics, were accused of unauthorised commercial use in residential buildings. The department took action against 11 properties on the final day of the drive.

stories.title: Signature Global bids for Raigad land parcel
stories.summary: Signature Global's subsidiary has emerged as the successful bidder for 475 acres of land in Raigad, Maharashtra, with a bid of 194.19 crore rupees. The company plans to expand its footprint beyond Gurugram into the Mumbai Metropolitan Region. The consortium will dilute 35 percent of its equity.

stories.title: Embassy Developments plans luxury Bengaluru project
stories.summary: Embassy Developments announced a new ultra-luxury residential project in Bengaluru with an estimated gross development value of 1,400 crore rupees. The project will feature 59 homes ranging up to 15,000 square feet. The company intends to integrate luxury hospitality services into the homeownership experience for its residents.

stories.title: Peninsula Land signs Versova redevelopment deal
stories.summary: Peninsula Land has signed an agreement to redevelop two housing societies in Mumbai's Versova. The 1.5-acre project has an estimated gross development value of up to ₹775 crore. The company is part of the Ashok Piramal Group and intends to consolidate the land parcel for residential use.

stories.title: M3M and Jacob & Co. plan Gurugram luxury project
stories.summary: M3M India and luxury watchmaker Jacob & Co. have partnered for a residential project in Gurugram. The development involves a ₹1,650 crore investment and is projected to generate ₹3,300 crore in revenue. The project features 120 residences with prices starting at ₹26 crore per unit.

stories.title: Study calls for India-specific home price index
stories.summary: A study by Square Yards and IIM Bangalore suggests current methods for measuring home prices are ill-suited to India's data constraints. Researchers reviewed six global approaches and identified spatiotemporal modeling as the most viable option. The findings highlight the difficulty of applying mature market metrics to local data.

stories.title: K Raheja Corp signs 165-acre Panvel township deal
stories.summary: K Raheja Corp has signed a development agreement for a 165-acre mixed-use township in Panvel near Mumbai. The project holds a development potential of 1.24 crore sq ft and is valued at ₹956.05 crore. The developer secured a 76 percent revenue share from the landowner family.

stories.title: Louis Kahn theatre reopens in Indiana
stories.summary: The Arts United Center in Fort Wayne, Indiana, has reopened following a renovation by MKM Architecture + Design. Designed by Louis Kahn and opened in 1973, it remains the only theatre the architect ever completed. The project aimed to refresh the original structure while complementing Kahn's design.

stories.title: Studio Gang, Olin complete Women’s Leadership Center - The Architect’s Newspaper
Architect challenges Melbourne public housing demolition
stories.summary: Architect Simon Robinson is campaigning against the Victorian government's plan to demolish 44 public housing towers by 2051. Officials claim the buildings have reached the end of their useful lives. Robinson argues that retrofitting the existing structures is a smarter approach than total redevelopment.

stories.title: SOM completes first phase of Philadelphia station restoration
stories.summary: Architecture studio SOM has finished the initial phase of renovating the William H Gray III 30th Street Station in Philadelphia. The project focused on the 1930s main train hall. Because the building is on the National Register of Historic Places, the studio was limited in its design changes.

stories.title: COLECTIVO C733 wins inaugural Siza Award
stories.summary: Mexico-based COLECTIVO C733 has received the first Siza Award, established by the Serralves Foundation to honor socially responsible public architecture. The collective will receive €50,000 for work demonstrating sensitivity to local communities and public space. The award is intended for practices focused on the common good.

stories.title: Ring-of-Bjolfur installation completes in Iceland
stories.summary: Arkibygg Architects and Esja Architecture have completed the Ring-of-Bjolfur, a silver-toned circle installed on a mountain ridge in Iceland. The project translates a local Viking legend into a geometric form. The architects chose to leave the ring as a permanent marker on the landscape.

stories.title: Mallorcan townhouse listed for €1.55 million
stories.summary: A 1900 stone townhouse in the village of Biniali, Mallorca, has been listed for €1.55 million. The 290sqm property features restored historic elements including exposed stone walls and timber-beamed ceilings. A dark steel staircase has been added to contrast with the building's original masonry.

stories.title: SSdH transforms Melbourne warehouse
stories.summary: Architecture practice SSdH has converted a former warehouse in Melbourne into a residence and exhibition space. The studio added a double-height glass atrium and a steel-mesh stair tower to increase natural light. The design prioritizes adaptation of the existing structure over total replacement.

stories.title: Construction progresses on Shenzhen Opera House
stories.summary: Ateliers Jean Nouvel has released construction photos of the Shenzhen Opera House, which is scheduled for completion in 2028. The 250,000-square-metre facility will feature an elongated roofscape designed to mirror the nearby sea. The venue will include a concert hall, a theatre, and an additional performance space.

stories.title: HTA Design finishes Greenwich housing project
stories.summary: HTA Design has completed a 452-home social rent development in Greenwich. The second phase of the project includes eight buildings ranging from six to fifteen storeys. The homes were delivered six years after the initial planning submission and are designed to exceed standard space requirements.

stories.title: Grape-picker cabins approved for wine estate
stories.summary: The South Downs National Park Authority has approved plans for six overnight cabins at the Rathfinny Wine Estate. The structures will be built within a former chalk quarry. The project also includes converting existing barns into a restaurant and terrace for the family-owned vineyard.

stories.title: Mario Pani's CUPA complex remains a landmark
stories.summary: Designed by Mario Pani and opened in 1949, the CUPA housing complex in Mexico City was a departure from original guidelines. The architect opted for a 13-story design with communal spaces and over a thousand apartments. It remains a notable example of Latin American functionalist architecture.

stories.title: Heidelberg Materials UK launches digital training
stories.summary: Heidelberg Materials UK has introduced a series of digital CPD sessions. The program is designed to provide expert-led guidance on sustainable construction practices to a broader audience.

stories.title: Researchers turn simulated moon dust into 3D-printed bricks
stories.summary: Researchers at the University of Arkansas have developed a method to 3D print interlocking bricks from simulated moon dust. The process uses heat to fuse the material without adhesives or cement. The team suggests this could allow future lunar settlements to be built using materials gathered on-site.

stories.title: Adidas headquarters expansion uses specialized glass for daylighting
stories.summary: The 460,000-square-foot Adidas headquarters expansion in Portland features curtainwall and punched windows using Solarban R67 and Solarban 60 Acuity glasses. Designed by LEVER Architecture, the five-story LEED Gold project includes a maker lab, offices and a lobby with a living green wall flanking a soccer field.

stories.title: ICON begins 12,649 sq ft commercial project in Texas
stories.summary: Construction company ICON has started 3D printing a 12,649 square-foot exhibition and training center for ASCO Equipment in San Antonio. The project combines robotically printed walls with a 60 ton steel superstructure to accommodate heavy machinery. Completion is scheduled for summer 2027.

stories.title: Mineralized biochar enables carbon-negative cement pastes
stories.summary: Researchers have demonstrated that modifying bamboo biochar with industrial carbide slag allows cement pastes to reach net carbon-negative status at replacement levels above twenty percent. The study, published in Low-carbon Materials and Green Construction, notes this approach mitigates setting delays and mechanical penalties common in raw biochar mixtures.

stories.title: Tripo AI previews H3.5 model and Polipop agent
stories.summary: Tripo AI has previewed its H3.5 generative model and Polipop agent at Formnext 2026. The company positions these tools as a bridge between AI-generated content and 3D printers. The H3.5 model is marketed as a 3D native foundation model designed to produce print-ready output.

stories.title: China engineers pioneer 3D-printed load-bearing aircraft structures
stories.summary: Engineers at the Shenyang Aircraft Design and Research Institute have used metal 3D printing to create primary load-bearing structures for military aircraft. The 16.4-foot component was produced using segmented printing and fusion techniques. China has been developing these manufacturing capabilities for over two decades.

stories.title: Hütt 01 Passivhaus features sustainable timber flooring
stories.summary: The Hütt 01 Passivhaus in Melbourne, a project by architects Felicity and Marc Bernstein, incorporates various sustainable building materials. The home features Havwoods HW9554 Abrego timber flooring from the company's Venture Plank range. The residence is designed to meet Passivhaus standards for energy efficiency.

stories.title: Raise3D increases RMS220 printer capacity
stories.summary: Raise3D has released software and firmware updates that increase the Z-axis build height of its RMS220 SLS 3D printer from 350 mm to 450 mm. The company states this change provides a capacity increase of nearly 30 percent without requiring hardware retrofits.

stories.title: CNH Industrial to sell 70% stake in equipment business
stories.summary: CNH Industrial plans to sell a 70 percent stake in its equipment business to Kobelco Construction Machinery, valuing the venture at $1 billion. The company will retain a 30 percent stake as it shifts its focus toward agricultural technology, services and precision farming equipment.

stories.title: Boom Supersonic orders ceramic 3D printers for turbine blades
stories.summary: Boom Supersonic has ordered three Lithoz CeraFab S65 printers to produce casting cores for turbine blades. The company aims to move blade production in-house, though it has not disclosed yield results. The casting process remains a factor for the company's 2027 turbine delivery targets.

stories.title: Carbon-negative building materials market enters growth phase
stories.summary: A report from IndexBox indicates that the global market for carbon-negative building materials is entering a high-growth phase. The construction sector is shifting toward active atmospheric carbon removal using materials like biochar insulation, hempcrete, carbon-cured concrete and cross-laminated timber to achieve net-negative footprints.

stories.title: Migrants and elephants compete for space on Teesta sandbars
stories.summary: Migrant farmers on the Teesta river's shifting sandbars are increasingly encountering elephants attracted to their seasonal crops. Floods and erosion force farmers to relocate fields, while elephants follow the food source. Farmers report crop and property damage but currently receive no formal compensation for their losses.

stories.title: IIT Delhi ranks first in India for sustainability
stories.summary: IIT Delhi has secured the top position in India and entered the global top 200 in the QS World University Rankings: Sustainability 2027. The institute improved its global standing to 194th place and increased its sustainability score to 86.5, citing progress in renewable energy and waste management.

stories.title: Experts propose AI to monitor smart city pollution
stories.summary: Experts at a seminar in Varanasi suggested that smart city planning should integrate AI, sensors and data systems to monitor pollution and climate risks. The discussion emphasized combining modern technology with traditional knowledge to protect urban rivers, lakes and green spaces during infrastructure development.

stories.title: Three firms selected for 3D city reconstruction project
stories.summary: IN-SPACe has selected SpacePixxel Technologies, KaleidEO Space Systems and Azista Industries to develop high-resolution 3D reconstruction techniques for Indian cities. The companies will receive a collective seed fund of 1.46 crore to demonstrate satellite-based systems for mapping the built environment using monocular imagery.

stories.title: Indian Railways upgrades fog safety systems
stories.summary: Indian Railways has upgraded its Fog Safety Device signalling system on several routes to mitigate winter delays. The system is intended to assist loco pilots in spotting signals during dense fog, which often forces speed restrictions and disrupts train schedules across North India.

stories.title: IN-SPACe funds 3D city mapping initiative
stories.summary: The Indian space agency IN-SPACe has awarded 1.46 crore in seed funding to three private firms to develop satellite-based 3D city reconstruction. SpacePixxel Technologies, KaleidEO Space Systems and Azista Industries will work on indigenous systems to map human settlements under the agency's demonstration scheme.

stories.title: Space regulator selects firms for urban geospatial mapping
stories.summary: IN-SPACe has selected three Indian space companies to develop high-resolution 3D mapping of human settlements. The initiative aims to provide Niti Aayog with detailed geospatial data for urban planning, infrastructure development and disaster risk assessment. The firms will receive 1.46 crore in collective seed funding.

stories.title: IN-SPACe selects 3 space companies for urban mapping
stories.summary: IN-SPACe has selected SpacePixxel, KaleidEO and Azista Industries to develop high-resolution settlement layers using Indian satellite data. The three companies will receive a collective 1.46 crore rupees to test the technology in Bengaluru and Shimla. The project aims to map human settlements from orbit.

stories.title: University of Leeds studies urban heat in Pune
stories.summary: Researchers from the University of Leeds are partnering with local institutions in Pune to study how extreme heat affects residents in informal settlements. The project aims to identify sustainable cooling solutions for communities vulnerable to rising temperatures. The heat is currently being studied.

stories.title: Green Bengal Summit examines climate-ready infrastructure
stories.summary: Policymakers and urban planners met at the CII IGBC Green Bengal Summit 2026 to discuss water management, green buildings and climate-ready infrastructure. Discussions focused on mitigating urban challenges like waterlogging and rising temperatures as West Bengal cities continue to expand. The weather remains a topic of conversation.

stories.title: Panaji plans second smart road for 38 crore rupees
stories.summary: Imagine Panaji Smart City Development Ltd plans to convert a 1.4 kilometer stretch along Rua de Ourem into a smart road. The 38.2 crore rupee project includes underground utility ducts and storm drainage, with officials warning the construction could disrupt traffic for over a year.

stories.title: Free wildfire home assessments offered in California
stories.summary: The U.S. Green Building Council California is offering free property walkthroughs to identify wildfire risks for residents in high-hazard zones across Los Angeles and Orange counties. Staff will provide recommendations to help homeowners make their properties more resistant to fire. The advice is currently available.

stories.title: Public agencies seek to quantify resilient infrastructure
stories.summary: Public agencies are developing methods to assign economic and environmental values to nature-based infrastructure projects. The initiative aims to build a financial case for engineering solutions that provide community benefits. The value of nature is being calculated.

stories.title: Researchers map potential tree planting sites in San Antonio
stories.summary: UT San Antonio researchers are helping the city identify locations for 1,000 new trees as part of the Trees Everywhere initiative. The project aims to cool the urban core and improve walkability over the next decade. The downtown area is currently being surveyed for shade.

stories.title: UN-Habitat releases guide for El Niño preparedness
stories.summary: UN-Habitat and the Climate Prediction and Applications Centre have published a guide to help city governments prepare for El Niño. The climate pattern is expected to bring floods and heat waves through March 2027. The guide offers considerations for cities to improve their resilience.

stories.title: US cities face rising heat and medical risks
stories.summary: Climate change and the urban heat island effect have made all 50 of the largest U.S. cities hotter over the last 50 years. Researchers note that extreme heat is a growing threat to public health for the 260 million Americans living in urban areas.

stories.title: American Forests targets tree canopy gaps
stories.summary: American Forests is working with cities like Boynton Beach to plant trees and close canopy gaps to combat extreme heat. The organization notes that heat-related deaths are expected to increase tenfold by 2050 in the Eastern U.S. Trees are being positioned as a public health intervention.

stories.title: Global review details urban climate vulnerability
stories.summary: A literature synthesis published in City and Built Environment documents how infrastructure and governance dictate a city's ability to recover from climate extremes. The review highlights that urban centers are both drivers of climate change and highly vulnerable to its impacts. The findings are now synthesized.

stories.title: Neowise uses AI to turn 2D video into 3D
stories.summary: NeoWise is targeting construction and defense markets with software that converts 2D camera footage into 3D environments. The company claims its technology can identify objects in low light and help drones read terrain without additional sensors. The 3D world is being rendered from 2D video.

stories.title: TimberBLDR appoints new president for US expansion
stories.summary: TimberBLDR has appointed Simon Siegert as president to lead its mass timber construction expansion across the United States. The company, part of the BLDR Holdings portfolio, focuses on design and installation services. The leadership team is now being strengthened.

VSBLTY enters India surveillance market
stories.summary: VSBLTY Groupe Technologies has partnered with QuadGen Wireless Solutions to deploy AI surveillance software in Indian smart city projects. The agreement aims to tap into the local public safety market while navigating new domestic manufacturing requirements. The software is being prepared for deployment.

stories.title: Pegasus and Taisei launch 150 million dollar construction fund
stories.summary: Pegasus Tech Ventures and Taisei Corporation have established a 150 million dollar corporate venture capital fund to invest in construction startups. The ten-year initiative will focus on robotics, AI and digital twins. The future of construction is being funded.

stories.title: IN-SPACe funds 3D mapping startups
stories.summary: IN-SPACe has selected three Indian space companies to develop 3D reconstruction technologies for mapping human settlements. SpacePixxel, KaleidEO, and Azista Industries will receive 1.46 crore in seed funding to build a system using monocular imagery. The initiative aims to reconstruct India’s built environment from satellite data.

stories.title: Promise Robotics raises $28M to scale robotic homebuilding - Dealroom
Promise Robotics raises $40 million for automated homebuilding
stories.summary: Toronto-based Promise Robotics has raised $40 million to scale its automated approach to homebuilding. The company uses AI to break dwelling designs into components for robotic assembly, aiming to address productivity growth and skilled labor shortages. The construction sector is now being told it needs more industrial capacity.

stories.title: Fermat raises $8 million for AI fashion design
stories.summary: Barcelona-based Fermat has raised $8 million in seed funding to expand its AI platform from design tools to full garment production. The company claims explosive growth and near-zero customer churn. It plans to open a New York office to support its software used by brands like J.Crew.

Finnish startup raises €3.5 million pre-seed to bring AI to data centre construction sites - ArcticStartup - ArcticStart
Fermat expands AI fashion software to factory production
stories.summary: Fermat has raised $8 million to expand its AI fashion platform, including a new tool that turns designs into factory-ready specifications. The startup, which launched in 2022, is used by more than 350 customers. It intends to use the capital to open a New York office.

stories.title: Rethinking accessibility in architectural education
stories.summary: Assistant professor Andrew Gipe-Lazarou is integrating the lived experiences of people with disabilities into architectural education. His approach encourages students to view accessibility as a starting point for innovation rather than a regulatory checklist. The curriculum aims to place human experience at the center of design.

stories.title: Penn State School of Music receives $6.2 million bequest
stories.summary: Dan and Eleanor Armstrong have committed $6.2 million to the Penn State School of Music. The gift follows their four-decade tenure at the institution. The funds are intended to sustain the school’s music education programs and support its mission of preparing musicians and educators for their communities.

stories.summary: At Tuskegee University in Tuskegee, Alabama, there is tradition grounded in collaboration and partnership. We have historically explored these traditions through education and architecture, to expand opportunities for students to shape the world beyond the classroom. stories.title: MoMA to host exhibition on 1980s and 1990s design
stories.summary: The Museum of Modern Art will open Bold Is Better: ’80s and ’90s Design on January 17. The exhibition features nearly 150 works from the museum’s collection, including furniture, fashion, and technology. It explores narrative in postmodern design and the influence of popular culture on the era's aesthetic.

stories.title: Student work showcased at 2x8: RECLAIM exhibition
stories.summary: The annual 2x8: RECLAIM exhibition opens November 19 in Los Angeles, featuring student architecture and interior design projects from across California. Organized by AIA Los Angeles and Architecture for Communities Los Angeles, the event provides scholarship opportunities while asking students to consider what architecture can take back for the public.

stories.title: IIM Bangalore earns IGBC Platinum Green Campus certification
stories.summary: IIM Bangalore has become the first educational institution in India to receive Platinum certification under the Indian Green Building Council’s Green Campus Rating System. The recognition acknowledges the institute’s commitment to energy efficiency and water management. The campus is now officially sustainable according to version 1.0.

stories.summary: VMPL Bengaluru (Karnataka) [India], November 17: The Open Group, the vendor-neutral technology standards organization, successfully concluded the INITIATE Conclave & Awards 2026 - Enterprise Architecture and Artificial Intelligence Fusion Day at the Wipro Kodathi Campus, Bengaluru, bringing together thought leaders, industry experts, academia, and emerging architects for a day focused

stories.title: Jantar Mantar loses its status as a protest site
stories.summary: Jantar Mantar was denotified as a protest site on 11 October 2026. The site was built nearly 300 years ago as an architectural instrument to measure the heavens and produce scientific knowledge. It has spent the last three decades serving as a hub for public demonstrations.

research.title: A material just one atom thick reveals a strange quantum secret
research.summary: Researchers at the University of Osaka have discovered a remarkable quantum state forming at the boundary between a one-atom-thick material and a metal. They observed electrons behaving as though they were unusually heavy, including a previously unseen state created by interactions between the ultrathin layer and the copper.

research.title: How to Agree Without Agreeing
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Consensus lets institutions decide without a central authority, but a record of agreement reveals neither its basis nor its credibility. We model support, standing aside and veto as responses to a proposal. A proposal can pass. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Intransigence or compromise: concatenated opinion dynamics with voting feedback
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study opinion evolution in a sequence of Friedkin-Johnsen (FJ) models, concatenated so that the final opinions of each model serve as the initial opinions of the next. Each FJ model is followed. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Logarithmic dispersion at marginal stability in collective attention
research.summary: Announce Type: replace Abstract: How cross-sectional heterogeneity evolves in nonequilibrium populations of competing, ageing units is a collective question that cannot be resolved from a representative trajectory or the ensemble mean alone. Analysis of more than two million age-aligned English. Preprint, not peer reviewed.
